assertion_results.text: The plan detects that the proposed uniqueness assertion in Test Requirements conflicts with the per-row CPE Acceptance Criterion and fixture semantics
assertion_results.evidence: The plan has a top-level section titled 'Conflict Detected: Test Requirements vs. Acceptance Criteria and Fixture'. It explicitly states the uniqueness clause 'introduces a uniqueness constraint that the Acceptance Criteria do not state. This is an unstated contract constraint.' (line 15) and dedicates a subsection 'The Fixture Proves Uniqueness Is Wrong' (line 17) showing the conflict with fixture semantics.

assertion_results.text: The plan distinguishes the explicit acceptance criterion (a non-empty CPE on every image row) from global uniqueness
assertion_results.evidence: Lines 5-9 present 'The Acceptance Criterion (authoritative)' as 'Every image row includes a non-empty CPE value' and note 'This is a per-row presence requirement: each row must have a CPE, but nothing is said about values being distinct across rows.' Lines 13-15 separately present 'The Proposed Test Requirement (conflicts)' identifying uniqueness as a distinct, conflicting clause.

assertion_results.text: The plan cites the supplied fixture's api-rhel9 and api-rhel10 rows sharing the exact same CPE value as evidence that CPEs may repeat
assertion_results.evidence: Lines 19-26 contain a table showing api-rhel9 and api-rhel10 both with CPE 'cpe:2.3:a:example:trustify_api:2.1.0:*:*:*:*:*:*:*'. The plan states: 'api-rhel9 and api-rhel10 are different components (one targets RHEL 9, the other RHEL 10) but share the same product version (2.1.0) and therefore the same CPE.' and 'Multiple image rows can and do legitimately share a CPE.'

assertion_results.text: The plan flags the proposed uniqueness condition as an unsupported contract constraint and contradictory to the fixture
assertion_results.evidence: Line 15: 'This is an unstated contract constraint.' Lines 29-31: '1. Contradict the fixture — the assertion would fail against the very data it is supposed to validate. 2. Add a constraint the contract does not require — the Acceptance Criteria say "non-empty," not "unique."' Line 39: 'The proposed uniqueness clause is rejected.'

assertion_results.text: The plan proposes a corrected assertion that requires a CPE on each row while allowing duplicate values
assertion_results.evidence: Lines 48-49 state the corrected assertion: 'Every image row has a non-empty CPE value.' Lines 51-53 confirm: 'Satisfies the Acceptance Criterion... Passes against the supplied fixture (both rows have a CPE, even though they share the same value). Does not introduce constraints beyond what the contract requires.'

assertion_results.text: The plan does not change the fixture values or implement uniqueness merely because the Test Requirements proposed it
assertion_results.evidence: Lines 60-62 explicitly state: 'The supplied fixture values (api-rhel9 and api-rhel10 sharing cpe:2.3:a:example:trustify_api:2.1.0:*:*:*:*:*:*:*) are semantically correct and remain unchanged. The plan does not alter fixture data to satisfy an invalid assertion.' The corrected assertion on line 49 removes the uniqueness check entirely.
